rationale: The BOOK ENTRY's core identification — the Name as the covenant identity of a house, constituted by the Head's Word, covenant law, and fruitful priesthood — is carried directly by the specific chain of supplied texts: the ark is expressly 'called by the name of the LORD' (2 Sam 6:2); the temple is a 'house for my name' built precisely to hold that ark 'wherein is the covenant of the LORD' (2 Sam 7:13; 1 Kgs 8:20-21); Hebrews 9:4 inventories the ark's three contents; and Scripture itself defines each content in the cited verses (manna = every word from the mouth of the LORD, Deut 8:3; tables = the declared covenant of ten commandments, Deut 4:13; Aaron's budded rod = the God-chosen priesthood, Num 17:5, 8). Isaiah 4:1 supplies the house/marriage mechanics of bearing a name while refusing the head's provision, which grounds the entry's 'in vain' clause alongside Ex 20:7. The strongest counter — the common character/presence reading, including Deuteronomistic name-theology — agrees that a name signifies identity, character, and authority, and so does not contradict the entry's core referent; it merely leaves the entry's distinctive evidence (why the ark bears the Name and why its three defined contents sit inside the house built 'for my name') unexplained as incidental memorials. No supplied text is explained by the counter that the book's core cannot explain without contradiction: even 'dwelleth between the cherubims' is compatible with the Head dwelling over His own covenant. Under inference to the best explanation of the supplied evidence, the book entry wins, and every material assertion printed in the entry (core identification, counterfeit-by-substitution, in-vain-by-rejection) has supporting evidence in the printed references and chapter (Ex 20:7 with Ezek 36:20-23 and Deut 28:58; Gen 11:4 vs 12:2 and Rev 13:17 vs 14:1 for the counterfeit clause).
book_core_identification: A Name is the covenant identity of a house (a head joined to a people), whose substance is the Head's Word, the Head's covenant law, and the Head's fruitful (God-appointed) priesthood — the three items Scripture places in the ark over which the Name is called and around which the house for the Name is built.
book_secondary_elaborations: Substituting any one of the three constituents (Word, covenant law, fruitful priesthood) with a rival supplied under another head creates a counterfeit Name.
Rejecting, replacing, or removing any one of the three constituents while still claiming the Name is what it means to take the Name in vain (Ex 20:7).
chapter_only_objections: The reading of John 14:13-14 ('whatsoever ye shall ask in my name') as resolved by house-membership rather than by other standard qualifications (e.g., 1 John 5:14 alone) is a chapter-level application, not asserted in the entry.

The mapping of the Lord's Prayer petitions onto manna/covenant/priesthood (daily bread = manna-Word, debts = covenant release, deliverance = priestly intercession) is an extended typological application that outruns the printed references.
The interpretation of Matthew 7:21-23 ('Lord, Lord... I never knew you') as the paradigm case of an emptied Name is a chapter argument, plausible but not required by the entry.
The marriage-subjection application (Eph 5:23-24; 1 Pet 3:5-6; Ezek 16:8; Num 15:38-40 tassels-as-covering) extends the symbol into household ethics beyond the glossary claim.
The framing of Isaiah 4:1's seven women as 'the marriage form of Lord, Lord' is an inferential parallel; the verse itself shows only name-claiming without provision.
The eschatological forehead contrast (Rev 13:17 vs 14:1) and the Acts 4:12 explanation ('no other Head supplies the Word, covenant, and priesthood') are chapter-level extensions.
The method excerpt's reading of Daniel 12:4 as modern search tooling is a hermeneutical aside irrelevant to the entry.
strongest_counter_interpretation: The composite common reading: 'name' signifies the character, identity, authority, and manifest presence of its bearer; in the Deuteronomistic texts the LORD causes His Name to dwell in the sanctuary as a mode of His presence (name-theology), so the temple is a 'house for my name' because God's presence is enthroned there 'between the cherubims,' not because of the ark's contents. On this reading the manna, tables, and rod are covenant memorials or 'testimonies' (kept 'before the testimony'), not constituents of the Name, and taking the Name in vain concerns false, empty, or profane invocation of God's name (oaths, hypocritical conduct) rather than a specific three-part rejection.
counter_core_identification: The Name is the revealed character, reputation, authority, and dwelling presence of the person (supremely God/Christ) — a person-centered symbol whose sanctuary usage denotes divine presence, with the ark's contents functioning as memorials rather than as the Name's substance.
material_core_denial: To genuinely rival the entry, the counter would have to deny that the Name is the covenant identity of a house constituted by the ark's three contents — insisting instead that the Name is solely the bearer's character/presence and that the ark's inventory is incidental to why the Name is called over it. The supplied texts do not force that denial: 1 Kgs 8:21 identifies the ark's contents as 'the covenant of the LORD,' housed in the house built 'for the name,' which is exactly the entry's linkage.
counter_case: 2 Sam 6:2 ties the Name to the LORD 'that dwelleth between the cherubims' — a locational, presence-oriented phrase above the mercy seat, not a reference to the contents inside the ark.
Deut 12:5, 11 and 1 Kgs 8:27-29 (name-theology) treat the Name dwelling in the sanctuary as a mode of divine presence, which explains 'house for my name' without any appeal to the ark's inventory.
Ex 20:7 is historically read as prohibiting false or empty invocation (especially false oaths), a reading that requires no three-constituent structure.
The ark's contents are elsewhere styled memorials/witnesses ('before the testimony,' Num 17:10; Ex 16:33-34), suggesting commemorative rather than constitutive function.
The broad canonical usage (Ex 34:5-7; Ps 9:10; Phil 2:9-11) centers the name on the person's character and authority, not on institutional constituents.
book_explanatory_advantages: It explains why Scripture calls the ark itself by the Name (2 Sam 6:2) and why the house 'for my name' is defined by having 'set there a place for the ark, wherein is the covenant' (1 Kgs 8:20-21) — the Name/house/ark/covenant linkage is explicit in the cited verses, not imported.

It explains why the ark holds exactly three items (Heb 9:4) and why each item carries a prior explicit scriptural definition (Deut 8:3; Deut 4:13; Num 17:5, 8) — the common reading has no account of why the ark's inventory would sit under the term 'name' at all.

It explains the mechanics of Isaiah 4:1: women claiming a man's name while keeping their own bread and apparel — name-bearing as entry into a house under a head's provision, and name-claiming-without-substance as the 'in vain' pattern.
It unifies Ex 20:7 with Deut 28:58 and Ezek 36:20-23 (chapter evidence), where profaning/fearing the Name is tied to conduct under the law, not to speech alone.

It explains the counterfeit pattern (Gen 11:4 'let us make us a name' vs Gen 12:2 'I will make thy name great'; Rev 13:17 vs 14:1) as rival houses under rival heads, matching the entry's substitution clause.
counter_explanatory_advantages: It more naturally reads 'dwelleth between the cherubims' (2 Sam 6:2) as presence enthroned above the ark rather than substance inside it.
It matches the dominant canonical and historical usage of 'name' as character/reputation/authority across texts not printed with the entry (Ex 34:5-7; Prov 22:1; Phil 2:9-11).
It requires fewer inferential steps for Ex 20:7 taken in isolation.
decisive_sources: 2 Samuel 6:2 (the ark 'whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts')
2 Samuel 7:13 with 1 Kings 8:20-21 (house built 'for my name'; the ark with 'the covenant of the LORD' set inside it)
Hebrews 9:4 (the ark's three contents: manna, Aaron's budded rod, tables of the covenant)
Deuteronomy 8:3 (manna defined as living by every word of the LORD)
Deuteronomy 4:13 (tables defined as the declared covenant)
Numbers 17:5, 8 (the budded rod as the God-chosen priesthood)
Isaiah 4:1 (claiming a name while refusing the head's bread and apparel)
unresolved_objections: The presence-oriented phrase 'dwelleth between the cherubims' (2 Sam 6:2) gives the name-theology reading a foothold the book absorbs but does not directly rebut.

The equation of 'in vain' specifically with rejecting/replacing/removing one of the three constituents is an inferential extension of Ex 20:7, supported by Isa 4:1, Deut 28:58, and Ezek 36 but not stated in any single verse.

Hebrews 9:4's inventory stands in tension with 1 Kings 8:9 (only the two tables in the ark at the temple's dedication), a canonical wrinkle the chapter does not address; it does not defeat the symbolic derivation but is left unhandled.
